reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 3, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: A shape is made from exactly one quarter of a circle. What is it called?
What shape has no corners and no straight sides?
A shape is made from exactly half of a circle. What is it called?
A shape is made from exactly half of a circle. What is it called?
What shape has no corners and no straight sides?
A shape is made from exactly half of a circle. What is it called?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Samples directly test naming all three named shapes: 'no corners and no straight sides' keys to circle, 'exactly one quarter of a circle' keys to quarter-circle, and 'exactly half of a circle' keys to half-circle across seeds 42-50.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency pairs 'represent AND describe', but all 6 samples (mcq and read_mcq alike) only ask students to identify/name a shape from a verbal description; none asks the student to actively represent (draw, trace, or select an image of) a circle, half-circle, or quarter-circle.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentences like 'A shape is made from exactly one quarter of a circle. What is it called?' use short, concrete phrasing well suited to Grade 2 Quarter 1 reading level.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the 6 samples uses the same definitional template ('What is it called?' / 'What shape has...'); there is no real-object framing (a coin, a pizza slice, a clock face) to vary the context in which circle-family shapes appear.

competency_alignment.rationale: The variation across seeds 42-50 (quarter-circle, circle, half-circle) is exactly the three shapes this competency names, never drifting into the composite-figure content that belongs to sibling node mat_g2_mg_q1_1.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This is a discrete shape-naming competency with fractional vocabulary (quarter, half) rather than a numeric range, and all samples stay within that stated conceptual scope.
